delta_explanation.146_to_145: GET /v2/conversations/{conversationId}/threads/{threadId}/original-source is documented on two pages, one per Accept header (application/json vs message/rfc822). delta_explanation.145_to_144: DELETE /v2/customers/{customerId} is documented on two pages, 'Delete Customer' and 'Delete Customer Asynchronously'. Their literal request lines DIFFER (/v2/customers/100 vs /v2/customers/100?async=true), so deduping on the literal example path misses it. Both pages declare the SAME templated path. async=true switches the response from 204 No Content to 202 Accepted; it is a query parameter, not a second endpoint. This is the exact defect class the captain flagged on lever-hiring: double-counting query-string variants.

findings: The sync/async customer delete collapse had a second-order trap: whichever page survives the dedup also names the write action. The async page won, which would have shipped a command called 'delete customer asynchronously' whose path performs the SYNC delete. The action is named for the ENDPOINT (delete_customer) and the async behaviour is exposed as an optional --async query flag with omit_when_absent, so collapsing the count loses no documented behaviour.

Not every Help Scout collection keys on 'id' - user statuses key on userId - so stream primary keys are taken from the record the provider actually returns. connectorgen validate caught the assumed 'id' as primary_key_missing.

'GET /v2/reports/*' was a single excluded wildcard row standing for 33 distinct report endpoints. All 33 are now enumerated as direct reads: a report is an aggregate over a time window, not a record collection, so modelling it as a stream would turn a bounded fixed-target read into an ETL.

A direct_read command needs NO operations.json entry: commandrunner.validateDirectReadCommand accepts exactly one GET api_surface endpoint plus an explicit output_policy. Only operation-backed reads go through the endpoint ledger. That is why 49 direct reads add zero ledger entries.

api_surface rows carry the DOCUMENTED path (/v2/...) while streams and writes carry base-relative paths. engine.normalizeDirectReadPathForBaseURL strips the base path prefix from a direct-read path, so /v2/... resolves correctly against a /v2 base - and /v3/... does not, which is exactly why the five v3 rows are blocked.
